headline: Best solar marketing agency in Delhi NCR: 10 questions to ask before you sign
card_title: How to choose a solar marketing agency in Delhi NCR
card_text: Ten questions to ask any solar marketing agency, the red flags that waste ad budget, and how retainer, pay-per-lead and hybrid pricing compare for installers and EPCs.
intro:
If you run a solar installation or EPC business, finding the best solar marketing agency in Delhi NCR is less about who has the slickest pitch deck and more about who understands how a rooftop sale actually happens: a homeowner sees an ad, checks your Google reviews, asks about the subsidy, waits for a site survey, compares three quotes and then decides. An agency that only reports clicks and impressions will never see most of that journey.

Search for solar marketing agencies and you mostly get installer pages and general agency directories, not much help deciding. This guide fills that gap. It gives you ten questions to ask on the first call, the red flags that should end the conversation, how the common pricing models compare, and the Delhi NCR knowledge any agency working for you should already have.

sections.h2: What the best solar marketing agency in Delhi NCR actually does
sections.html:
A solar marketing agency is not just a team that runs Facebook ads. For an installer or EPC, the job covers the whole path from first impression to booked site survey:

  • Trust: a Google Business Profile with recent reviews and real installation photos, and a website that answers subsidy, savings and warranty questions clearly.
  • Demand: Meta lead ads and click-to-WhatsApp ads for homeowners, Google Search ads for people already looking, and local SEO for "solar panel installation near me" searches.
  • Filtering: lead forms and call scripts that separate owners with a usable roof from tenants, students and people outside your service area.
  • Follow-up: a simple system so every enquiry gets a call or WhatsApp within minutes, and lost leads get a second try.
  • Reporting: numbers you can act on, such as cost per qualified enquiry, cost per site visit and installations per month.

An agency that only covers one of these won't fix the rest.

sections.h2: 10 questions to ask a solar marketing agency
sections.html:
Use these on the first call. Good agencies answer most of them without hesitation; vague answers tell you a lot.

  1. How many solar businesses have you worked with, and can I see the work? Ask for case studies or live examples, not a logo slide. Ask what the agency did, not just what the client achieved.
  2. What do you count as a qualified solar lead? The answer should mention homeowner, roof access, service area and roughly the monthly bill or system size. If it's "anyone who fills the form", the leads will be cheap and useless.
  3. Which number will you report every week? Look for cost per site visit or cost per qualified enquiry, not only cost per click.
  4. Who owns the ad accounts, pixel and page? They should be in your business name, with the agency added as a partner. You should keep everything if you part ways.
  5. How will you talk about the PM Surya Ghar subsidy? A careful agency quotes the current official figures, says eligibility depends on the scheme rules and never writes "free solar".
  6. How do you split budget between Meta, Google and local SEO? There's no single right mix, but they should explain why for your business and city.
  7. What happens in the first 30, 60 and 90 days? Ask for a written plan with dates, not "we'll optimise as we go".
  8. How do you handle lead follow-up? Ask whether they set up WhatsApp replies, a lead sheet or CRM, and whether they review call outcomes with your team.
  9. Do you understand residential and commercial solar separately? A society, factory or school buys very differently from a kothi owner, with longer cycles and more decision-makers.
  10. What's the notice period and what do I get if I leave? Long lock-ins with nothing handed over are a warning sign.

sections.h2: Red flags to walk away from
sections.html:
• Guaranteed rankings or guaranteed leads. Nobody controls Google's results or Meta's auction. An agency can promise a process and honest reporting, not an outcome.
  • A per-lead price that sounds too good. Very cheap leads usually come from loose forms, wide targeting or incentivised clicks. Ask how many of those leads became site visits for other clients.
  • Ads that promise free electricity or a government partnership. These bring angry calls, policy problems on ad platforms and a dent in your reputation.
  • Ad accounts in the agency's name. If they own the account, they own your history and your audiences.
  • No questions about your sales team. If they never ask who calls the leads and how fast, they are planning to hand you a spreadsheet and walk away.
  • Reports full of reach and impressions. They say nothing about installations.

Most of these also apply when you choose any marketing partner. Our general checklist for choosing a digital marketing agency in Delhi NCR covers the wider points.

Whatever the model, your ad budget is usually separate from the agency fee and is paid to Google or Meta directly. Check whether the quote you're comparing includes or excludes ad spend and GST.

ModelHow it worksWorks well whenWatch out for
Fixed monthly retainerA set fee for agreed work: ads, creatives, GBP, reportingYou want a steady partner and predictable costsVague scope; ask exactly what's included each month
Percentage of ad spendThe fee rises with your budgetLarge budgets across several platformsAn incentive to raise spend rather than cut waste
Pay per leadYou pay for each enquiry deliveredShort tests, or when you only want leadsLoose definitions of a lead; quantity over quality

Whichever you choose, judge the agency on cost per site visit and installations, not on the fee alone. A cheaper agency that brings leads your team can't close is the expensive one.

sections.h2: Delhi NCR knowledge a solar agency should already have
sections.html:
Delhi NCR is not one market. It spans three states, several DISCOMs and very different kinds of homes. Before you sign, check that the agency can talk about:

  • Who supplies power where. In Delhi it's BSES Rajdhani, BSES Yamuna, Tata Power-DDL or NDMC depending on the area. Gurugram and Faridabad fall under DHBVN in Haryana. Noida and Ghaziabad are served by PVVNL, while much of Greater Noida is served by Noida Power Company (NPCL). Net-metering steps and timelines differ, and ads or landing pages that explain the right process for each area build trust.
  • State rules on top of the central scheme. PM Surya Ghar gives the same central subsidy across the country, but Delhi, Haryana and Uttar Pradesh have their own policies and incentives that change over time. Ad copy should be written per state and checked before every campaign.
  • Different buyers. Independent houses and kothis in South and West Delhi, high-rise societies in Gurugram, Noida and Greater Noida West, and industrial units in Faridabad, Manesar and Ghaziabad all need different targeting, creatives and sales conversations. In a society, for example, the roof usually belongs to the RWA, so an individual flat owner is rarely the buyer.
  • Local search behaviour. Many homeowners search with a locality name ("solar installer in Dwarka", "rooftop solar Sector 50 Gurgaon"), so Google Business Profile coverage and locality pages matter.

An agency that treats "Delhi NCR" as one radius on a map will waste budget on enquiries your team can't serve. Our guide to getting solar leads in Delhi NCR goes deeper on the local channel mix.

sections.h2: What a fair first 90 days looks like
sections.html:
1. Weeks 1–2: groundwork. Audit your Google Business Profile, website and any past ads. Set up tracking, the lead sheet or CRM, WhatsApp replies and a review request process.
  2. Weeks 3–6: first campaigns. Launch Meta lead ads and a small Google Search campaign for your core service areas, with qualifying questions on every form. Review call outcomes with your team every week.
  3. Weeks 7–12: tighten and scale. Cut the areas, ads and keywords that bring unqualified leads, add proof such as installation videos and reviews, and raise budget only on what produces site visits.

By the end you should know your real cost per site visit by channel and city. That number, not a promise, is what tells you whether to keep the agency. For more on what leads cost and where they come from, see our solar lead generation guide.

faqs: How do I choose the best solar marketing agency in Delhi NCR?

Ask for real solar case studies, how they define a qualified lead, which number they report weekly, who owns the ad accounts and what the first 90 days look like. Prefer agencies that measure cost per site visit and know the differences between Delhi, Haryana and UP.
How much does a solar marketing agency charge in India?

It depends on the model: a fixed monthly retainer, a percentage of ad spend, pay per lead or a hybrid. Ad budget is usually separate. Compare quotes on what's included and on expected cost per site visit, not just the fee.
Is pay per lead a good model for solar companies?

It can work for short tests, but only if a qualified lead is defined in writing, such as a homeowner in your service area with roof access. Without that, pay-per-lead deals tend to reward volume over quality.
Can a solar marketing agency guarantee leads or Google rankings?
No honest agency can guarantee rankings or results, because Google and Meta control their own systems. Look for a clear plan, transparent reporting and ownership of your accounts instead.
Should a solar agency handle both residential and commercial solar?

Only if it treats them separately. Homeowners respond to Meta and WhatsApp ads and quick site visits, while factories, schools and societies need longer sales cycles, proposals and more decision-makers.
